/-!
# Erdős Problem 487

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/487](https://www.erdosproblems.com/487)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta Arithmetica
  (1936), 147-151.
- [Kl71] Kleitman, Daniel, *Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union*.
  Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos487

/--
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ have positive density. Must there exist distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such
that $[a,b]=c$ (where $[a,b]$ is the least common multiple of $a$ and $b$)?

This is true, a consequence of the positive solution to [447] by Kleitman [Kl71].

Davenport and Erdős [DaEr36] showed that there must exist an infinite sequence $a_1<a_2\cdots$
in $A$ such that $a_i\mid a_j$ for all $i\leq j$, under the assumption that the upper logarithmic
density of $A$ is positive.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos487.lean"]
theorem erdos_487 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.HasPosDensity →
      ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c ∧ Nat.lcm a b = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos487

reformulations.difference: Lean requires one distinct LCM triple in each positive-density set. Erdős (1961), §II.1, also states the conclusion as infinitely many such triples; §I.26 uses the single-triple formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Deleting any finite initial segment preserves positive natural density. Apply the universally quantified single-triple statement to each remaining tail to obtain triples with all coordinates arbitrarily large, hence infinitely many triples. Conversely, infinitely many triples imply one. The universal single-triple and infinite-triple statements were proved equivalent in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the problem's sorry-backed theorem.

reformulations.difference: Lean permits sets of natural numbers containing 0, whereas the original number-theoretic setting uses positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A pairwise-distinct triple satisfying Nat.lcm a b = c automatically has a,b,c > 0: a zero input makes the output equal that input, and a zero output forces a zero input. Removing 0 preserves natural density. Thus restricting the quantified sets to exclude 0, or explicitly requiring positive witnesses, leaves the problem unchanged. Both equivalences were proved in the scratch file.

review.notes: The sole declaration matches the positive-natural-density question in Er61 §I.26. HasPosDensity requires an existing positive density; Er65b explicitly gives a stronger positive-lower-density version, and these density hypotheses should not themselves be identified. Lean checks confirmed the density expansion, satisfiable examples, exclusion of finite sets, and LCM boundary cases. The linked proof establishes the stronger lower-density result; its statement implies the repository statement, and its two source files contain no sorry or custom axiom declarations. I did not rebuild its Lean 4.29.1 project. Direct requests to erdosproblems.com/487 and the Kl71 full text were blocked; comparison used the original papers, and current status was corroborated by the independent database. The reviewed file remains unchanged.
